title: Are archetypes associated with competitive usage?
question: Do stat strength, stat shape (role axes, descriptive clusters) or anomalies relate to Gen 9 National Dex usage, and does anything beyond BST help predict it?
methodology: Smogon chaos stats, gen9nationaldex-1630, mean of 2026-07..09. Fully evolved Pokémon legal in the format (banned tiers removed using Showdown formats-data; tiers never used as inputs). Exact-form matching. Spearman with 1,000-sample bootstrap 95% intervals; Kruskal-Wallis across descriptive clusters; 5-fold x10 repeated CV comparing BST-only vs stats+shares+types models.
interpretation: BST has a clear moderate link to usage (rho 0.512, 95% CI [0.443, 0.579]). Stat shape does not: role axes rho -0.006 and -0.024, descriptive clusters p = 0.80. Held-out prediction: BST-only Spearman 0.51; best richer model (full_ridge) 0.549 (gain +0.039, beats BST in 64% of folds). Near-identical stat profiles can differ ~25x in usage (Great Tusk vs Buzzwole), so abilities, moves and typing drive much of usage.
limitations: Usage is popularity, not win rate. 27% of usage is in forms outside the dataset (Megas, alternate and regional forms); Eviolite users (Chansey, Porygon2) are excluded as not fully evolved. Showdown tier file taken from the live repo, frozen by local cache. Only 29 Pokémon pass the 4.52% high-usage cutoff, so group comparisons are hints. Tests are exploratory.
